nb2_lite_1K.texto: The body of an executed prisoner hangs motionless from a wooden gallows in a prison yard, a white cloth hood over his head, the rope taut, his hands bound behind his back, his boots a few feet above the trapdoor that has just dropped open. Two uniformed prison guards stand at attention below the platform and a priest in a black cassock holds a closed prayer book, head bowed. Men of European descent with fair to olive skin, light to dark brown or black hair, varied eye colour and lean, labour-hardened builds. Stone-walled prison yard 1924, raw timber gallows with thirteen steps, high walls topped with iron spikes, muddy ground. Grey overcast morning light, flat and cold. Wide shot, eye-level, 35mm lens, deep depth of field. A grainy 35mm documentary photograph taken in 1924, with muted colors and slight underexposure, in a dark-history realist style. The image has a 16:9 aspect ratio. No readable text, no signage, no labels.
